q: Only concave and convex mirrors having _____ surfaces are used in most applications.
e: Only concave and convex mirrors having spherical surfaces are used in most applications. The physics in this sentence is built around spherical.

q: If the reflecting surface of a mirror forms part of the inner surface of a hollow sphere, it is a _____ mirror.
e: If the reflecting surface of a mirror forms part of the inner surface of a hollow sphere, it is a concave mirror. The physics in this sentence is built around concave.

q: If the reflecting surface of a mirror forms part of the outer surface of a hollow sphere, it is a _____ mirror.
e: If the reflecting surface of a mirror forms part of the outer surface of a hollow sphere, it is a convex mirror. The physics in this sentence is built around convex.

q: The centre of the surface of a concave or convex mirror is called its _____.
e: The centre of the surface of a concave or convex mirror is called its pole. A convex mirror diverges light and gives a wide field of view.

q: The centre of a sphere, part of whose surface is the mirror, is called the centre of _____.
e: The centre of a sphere, part of whose surface is the mirror, is called the centre of curvature. Curvature names the centre of a sphere, part of whose surface is the mirror,.

q: The centre of curvature of a concave mirror is in _____ of the reflecting surface.
e: The centre of curvature of a concave mirror is in front of the reflecting surface. A concave mirror can converge light to a real focus.

q: The centre of curvature of a convex mirror is _____ the reflecting surface.
e: The centre of curvature of a convex mirror is behind the reflecting surface. A convex mirror diverges light and gives a wide field of view.

q: The radius of the sphere, part of whose surface is the mirror, is called the radius of _____.
e: The radius of the sphere, part of whose surface is the mirror, is called the radius of curvature. Curvature names the radius of the sphere, part of whose surface is the mirror,.

q: The line passing through the centre of curvature and the pole is called the principal _____.
e: The line passing through the centre of curvature and the pole is called the principal axis. Axis names the line passing through the centre of curvature and the pole.

q: When rays parallel and close to the principal axis are incident on a concave mirror, the reflected rays pass through the principal _____.
e: When rays parallel and close to the principal axis are incident on a concave mirror, the reflected rays pass through the principal focus. A concave mirror can converge light to a real focus.

q: Since the reflected rays actually intersect at the focus, the focus of a concave mirror is a _____ focus.
e: Since the reflected rays actually intersect at the focus, the focus of a concave mirror is a real focus. A concave mirror can converge light to a real focus.

q: When rays parallel to the principal axis are incident on a convex mirror, the reflected rays appear to come from the principal _____.
e: When rays parallel to the principal axis are incident on a convex mirror, the reflected rays appear to come from the principal focus. A convex mirror diverges light and gives a wide field of view.

q: Since reflected rays do not actually pass through it, the principal focus of a convex mirror is a _____ focus.
e: Since reflected rays do not actually pass through it, the principal focus of a convex mirror is a virtual focus. A convex mirror diverges light and gives a wide field of view.

q: The distance between the pole and the focus of a mirror is called the _____ length.
e: The distance between the pole and the focus of a mirror is called the focal length. Focal names the distance between the pole and the focus of a mirror.

q: For rays close to the principal axis, the focal length $f$ is approximately equal to _____ of the radius of curvature $R$.
e: For rays close to the principal axis, the focal length $f$ is approximately equal to half of the radius of curvature $R$. The physics in this sentence is built around half.

q: When the object is at infinity, the image in a concave mirror is formed at _____.
e: When the object is at infinity, the image in a concave mirror is formed at F. A concave mirror can converge light to a real focus.

q: When the object is beyond C in a concave mirror, the image is formed between _____.
e: When the object is beyond C in a concave mirror, the image is formed between C and F. A concave mirror can converge light to a real focus.

q: When the object is at C in a concave mirror, the image is of the _____ size as the object.
e: When the object is at C in a concave mirror, the image is of the same size as the object. Same here means lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised.

q: When the object is between C and F in a concave mirror, the image is formed _____.
e: When the object is between C and F in a concave mirror, the image is formed beyond C. A concave mirror can converge light to a real focus.

q: When the object is at F in a concave mirror, the image is formed at _____.
e: When the object is at F in a concave mirror, the image is formed at infinity. A concave mirror can converge light to a real focus.

q: When the object is between F and P in a concave mirror, the image is formed _____ the mirror.
e: When the object is between F and P in a concave mirror, the image is formed behind the mirror. A concave mirror can converge light to a real focus.

q: The image formed in a convex mirror is always virtual, erect and _____ than the object.
e: The image formed in a convex mirror is always virtual, erect and smaller than the object. A convex mirror diverges light and gives a wide field of view.

q: The image in a convex mirror is formed between P and _____ no matter where the object is situated.
e: The image in a convex mirror is formed between P and F no matter where the object is situated. A convex mirror diverges light and gives a wide field of view.

q: Convex mirrors are used as rear view mirrors since they give an erect image and a _____ field of view.
e: Convex mirrors are used as rear view mirrors since they give an erect image and a wide field of view. The physics in this sentence is built around wide.

q: Concave mirrors are used as reflectors in motor car headlamps and as a _____ mirror to produce an enlarged image.
e: Concave mirrors are used as reflectors in motor car headlamps and as a shaving mirror to produce an enlarged image. The physics in this sentence is built around shaving.

q: According to sign conventions, distances of real object, real image and real focus are _____.
e: According to sign conventions, distances of real object, real image and real focus are positive. The physics in this sentence is built around positive.

q: According to sign conventions, distances of virtual object, virtual image and virtual focus are _____.
e: According to sign conventions, distances of virtual object, virtual image and virtual focus are negative. The physics in this sentence is built around negative.

q: The focal length and radius of curvature of a concave mirror are _____.
e: The focal length and radius of curvature of a concave mirror are positive. A concave mirror can converge light to a real focus.

q: The focal length and radius of curvature of a convex mirror are _____.
e: The focal length and radius of curvature of a convex mirror are negative. A convex mirror diverges light and gives a wide field of view.

q: The perpendicular distance measured above the principal axis is _____.
e: The perpendicular distance measured above the principal axis is positive. The physics in this sentence is built around positive.

q: The perpendicular distance measured below the principal axis is _____.
e: The perpendicular distance measured below the principal axis is negative. The physics in this sentence is built around negative.

q: The mirror formula relates object distance $u$, image distance $v$, and focal length $f$ as $1/u + 1/v = $ _____.
e: The mirror formula relates object distance $u$, image distance $v$, and focal length $f$ as $1/u + 1/v = $ $1/f$. The physics in this sentence is built around $1/f$.

q: The lateral magnification produced by a mirror is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the _____.
e: The lateral magnification produced by a mirror is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object. The physics in this sentence is built around object.

q: The magnification $m$ can also be expressed in terms of $v$ and $u$ as $m = $ _____.
e: The magnification $m$ can also be expressed in terms of $v$ and $u$ as $m = $ $-v/u$. The physics in this sentence is built around $-v/u$.

q: When the object is between F and P in a concave mirror, the image is virtual, erect, and _____ than the object.
e: When the object is between F and P in a concave mirror, the image is virtual, erect, and larger than the object. A concave mirror can converge light to a real focus.

q: In a concave mirror, when the object is between C and F, the image is real, inverted, and _____ than the object.
e: In a concave mirror, when the object is between C and F, the image is real, inverted, and larger than the object. A concave mirror can converge light to a real focus.

q: In a concave mirror, when the object is beyond C, the image is real, inverted, and _____ than the object.
e: In a concave mirror, when the object is beyond C, the image is real, inverted, and smaller than the object. A concave mirror can converge light to a real focus.

q: In a concave mirror, when the object is at infinity, the image is real, inverted and _____ than the object.
e: In a concave mirror, when the object is at infinity, the image is real, inverted and smaller than the object. A concave mirror can converge light to a real focus.

q: The minus sign in the magnification formula $m = -v/u$ determines both the nature and _____ of the image.
e: The minus sign in the magnification formula $m = -v/u$ determines both the nature and configuration of the image. The physics in this sentence is built around configuration.

q: Images of objects formed in plane and convex mirrors are always _____.
e: Images of objects formed in plane and convex mirrors are always virtual. The physics in this sentence is built around virtual.

q: The image formed in a concave mirror can be real or virtual depending on the _____ of the object.
e: The image formed in a concave mirror can be real or virtual depending on the position of the object. A concave mirror can converge light to a real focus.

q: All distances in the mirror formula are measured from the _____ of the mirror.
e: All distances in the mirror formula are measured from the pole of the mirror. The physics in this sentence is built around pole.

q: A ray of light is a path along which the light _____.
e: A ray of light is a path along which the light travels. Distance grows with the path, even if you return to the start involving which.

q: The arrow-head on a ray of light points in the direction of _____ of light.
e: The arrow-head on a ray of light points in the direction of propagation of light. The physics in this sentence is built around propagation. Reflection: light bouncing back from a surface.

q: The sun is the _____ source of light.
e: The sun is the chief source of light. The physics in this sentence is built around chief.

q: The speed of light has a _____ value.
e: The speed of light has a definite value. The physics in this sentence is built around definite. Variable: a quantity that can change, not the agreed measuring unit.

q: The image I in a plane mirror is observed as the reflected rays enter the _____.
e: The image I in a plane mirror is observed as the reflected rays enter the eye. The physics in this sentence is built around eye.

q: The points between O and O' on an extended object have the corresponding _____ between I and I'.
e: The points between O and O' on an extended object have the corresponding images between I and I'. The physics in this sentence is built around images.

q: When a man looks at his image in a looking glass and tilts his head right, the image tilts to the _____.
e: When a man looks at his image in a looking glass and tilts his head right, the image tilts to the left. The physics in this sentence is built around left.

q: A real image can be focused on a screen because it is formed by the actual _____ of reflected rays.
e: A real image can be focused on a screen because it is formed by the actual intersection of reflected rays. The physics in this sentence is built around intersection. Reflection: light bouncing back from a surface.

q: The minimum vertical length of a looking glass for a man to see his whole self is 2 ft 9 in if his height is 5 ft _____ in.
e: The minimum vertical length of a looking glass for a man to see his whole self is 2 ft 9 in if his height is 5 ft 6 in. The physics in this sentence is built around 6.

q: In an optical testing room, the letters are illuminated and _____ inverted.
e: In an optical testing room, the letters are illuminated and laterally inverted. The physics in this sentence is built around laterally.

q: A concave mirror may be used as a shaving mirror since it produces an _____ image.
e: A concave mirror may be used as a shaving mirror since it produces an enlarged image. A concave mirror can converge light to a real focus.

q: Convex mirrors have a _____ field of view than a plane mirror of the same size.
e: Convex mirrors have a wider field of view than a plane mirror of the same size. The physics in this sentence is built around wider.
